ann_34.text: This part acts on 165 of 242 training patients (68%), nearly all of them patients whose chest pain is not brought on by exercise.
For them it clearly lowers the risk (odds about 0.39 times on average, on the model's odds scale); 51 of these 165 patients had heart disease.
Through it, women have a lower risk than men, and even more so if exercise does not bring on chest pain.
Fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL lowers the risk here, and even more so if exercise does not bring on chest pain.
Chest pain brought on by exercise raises the risk through this part.

ann_36.text: This part adds risk only once serum cholesterol rises above about 285 mg/dL (7.4 mmol/L).
It acts on 9 of 242 training patients (4%), so the model has little data on this; for them the odds rise about 1.3 times on average, on the model's odds scale.
In the training data, 1 of these 9 patients had heart disease.

ann_37.text: Through this part, higher resting blood pressure clearly raises the risk (from 110 to 155 mm Hg, odds about 2.3 times, on the model's odds scale), the same size as its effect in the whole model.
Through the same part, higher cholesterol lowers the risk a little (odds about 0.63 times from 193 to 308 mg/dL, on the model's odds scale), offsetting part of cholesterol's overall rise.

ann_38.text: This part acts on 118 of 242 training patients (49%), and for them it clearly lowers the risk (odds about 0.42 times on average, on the model's odds scale).
These patients tend to have lower cholesterol and at most 1 vessel coloured; 23 of the 118 had heart disease.
Through it, more vessels coloured raise the risk, and even more so if the patient is a woman or has cholesterol at or below 240 mg/dL.
For patients with fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less, cholesterol adds risk through this part only while it stays below about 258 mg/dL (6.7 mmol/L).
For men, going from 0 to 1 vessel adds risk here, but more vessels add nothing further through this part.

ann_39.text: The model gives the biggest increase in risk to patients with more major vessels coloured by fluoroscopy: from 0 to 2 vessels, the odds rise about 176 times on average, on the model's odds scale.
Women get a much lower risk than men (odds about 0.04 times those of men, on the model's odds scale).
Compared with patients who have no chest pain symptoms, the model gives a much lower risk to patients with typical angina or non-anginal chest pain, and a lower risk to patients with atypical angina.
A flat ST segment at peak exercise clearly raises the risk compared with an upsloping one; a downsloping segment raises it too, but the model has little data on this (17 training patients).

Higher serum cholesterol (193 to 308 mg/dL), more ST depression on exercise (0 to 2.8 mm), chest pain brought on by exercise, a reversible defect on the thallium scan and higher resting blood pressure (110 to 155 mm Hg) each clearly raise the risk.
A higher maximum heart rate during exercise clearly lowers the risk, and so does fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL.
Older age raises the risk only slightly.

For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results, predicted risk 29%), the largest changes on the model's odds scale are about ×115 for 2 vessels instead of 0, about ×16 for a flat instead of an upsloping ST segment and about ×6 for cholesterol of 308 instead of 193 mg/dL.

The model has little data on three categories it treats strongly: a fixed defect on the thallium scan (15 patients, lower risk), an ST-T wave abnormality on the resting ECG (2 patients, higher risk) and a thallium result coded 4 (2 patients, much higher risk; the code is not defined).

ann_34.original: Node 155_a computes a 'benign profile' gate: 155_a = ReLU(0.824*sex:0 + 1.109*exang:0 - 0.509*fbs:0 + 0.088). Activates for female patients (sex:0=1) with no exertional angina (exang:0=1); normal fasting glucose slightly attenuates. Output-facing copy of hidden node 155. Activation profile: active 70% / hard-zero 30% (verified). Reads out to output with weight -0.960, lowering predicted risk. Ablation: removing this readout drops test AUC 0.897->0.869 (-0.028) - the single largest nonlinear contribution to generalisation.
ann_34.proposed: A part that acts on most patients without chest pain on exercise and lowers their risk, more for women and for patients with fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL.

ann_36.original: Node 3040 = ReLU(1.052*chol - 0.864): a one-sided cholesterol threshold. Since cholesterol is z-normalised, this turns on only above ~0.82 SD above the mean. Activation profile: hard-zero 82.5% / active 17.5% (verified) - a sparse threshold detector. Feeds node 534 with -0.677; net path effect +0.60 per unit (high cholesterol raises predicted risk). This is the sub-unit that lets cholesterol act as a risk factor only above a level rather than linearly - but it sits inside the 534 gate, which the ablation shows contributes nothing on test.
ann_36.proposed: Cholesterol above about 285 mg/dL (7.4 mmol/L) raises the risk; only 9 training patients are that high, and 1 of them had heart disease.

ann_37.original: Subgraph {trestbps, chol_c, 3240, 2379}: a near-linear resting-blood-pressure signal. 3240 = ReLU(0.978*trestbps + 3.4) is always-on (100% active, verified) - a linear pass-through, not a gate. 2379 = ReLU(0.931*3240 - 0.529*chol_c - 0.754) simplifies to ReLU(0.911*trestbps - 0.529*chol_c + 2.41), near-always-on. Reads out to output with +0.364 (higher resting BP raises risk). Ablation: removing this readout drops test AUC 0.897->0.885 (-0.012) - a modest but real generalising contribution.
ann_37.proposed: Higher resting blood pressure raises the risk through this part, while higher cholesterol lowers it a little.

ann_38.original: Node 534 = ReLU(0.818*[benign_profile_gate_534path] - 0.677*[chol_threshold] - 1.155*ca - 0.592*chol - 0.761): the model's most elaborate unit, a genuine ReLU gate (hard-zero 53.5% verified) composing four risk signals - vessel count (ca), a cholesterol copy, the cholesterol threshold (3040), and the redundant benign-profile copy (155_b). Net per-unit output effects: ca +1.02, chol +0.52, chol_threshold +0.60, benign -0.72; when the benign signal is strong the whole block is clipped off together. KEY ABLATION RESULT: disabling 534's readout changes test AUC only 0.897->0.899 (+0.002) while train drops 0.946->0.942 - i.e. this showpiece unit is essentially train-only and does not generalise. Signs match cardiology but the structure is fit to the 242 training cases.
ann_38.proposed: A part that lowers the risk for about half the patients, mostly those with lower cholesterol and at most one vessel coloured. Through it, more vessels raise the risk more for women, and cholesterol adds risk only up to about 258 mg/dL.

ann_39.original: Root: y0 = ReLU(bias 0.318 + linear core + 3 nonlinear pathways). (1) DIRECT LINEAR CORE of 17 inputs to the output - ca (largest, +2.03), cp:4 (+1.21), slope:2, chol, cp:2, oldpeak push risk up; sex:0 (-0.71), slope:1, thalach push down. By SHAP the top drivers are ca, cp:4, sex:0, slope:2, chol. (2) benign_profile_gate (155_a, -0.96) lowers risk for females without exertional angina. (3) restbp_chol_interaction (2379, +0.364). summary.text: The model's strongest signal is the number of major vessels coloured by fluoroscopy: going from 0 to 2 vessels multiplies the odds of heart disease by about 176 on average, on the model's odds scale.
Women get a much lower risk than men, and the gap is even wider for patients whose chest pain is not brought on by exercise.
Patients with typical angina or non-anginal chest pain get a much lower risk than patients with no chest pain symptoms.
A flat ST segment at peak exercise, higher cholesterol, more ST depression on exercise and higher resting blood pressure each clearly raise the risk, while a higher maximum heart rate lowers it.
One small part adds risk only once serum cholesterol rises above about 285 mg/dL (7.4 mmol/L), and it applies to just 9 training patients.

Worth checking: the model treats a fixed defect on the thallium scan as lowering the risk compared with a normal scan, from only 15 training patients.

Worth checking: the model gives a very high risk to the 2 training patients whose thallium result is coded 4, a code the dataset documentation does not define, and to the 2 patients with an ST-T wave abnormality on the resting ECG.
Worth checking: of the 9 patients in whom the high-cholesterol part adds risk, only 1 had heart disease.
Worth checking: through one part, higher cholesterol lowers the risk, which offsets part of its overall rise.

parts.name: benign_profile_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Node 155_a computes a 'benign profile' gate: 155_a = ReLU(0.824*sex:0 + 1.109*exang:0 - 0.509*fbs:0 + 0.088). Activates for female patients (sex:0=1) with no exertional angina (exang:0=1); normal fasting glucose slightly attenuates. Output-facing copy of hidden node 155. Activation profile: active 70% / hard-zero 30% (verified). Reads out to output with weight -0.960, lowering predicted risk. Ablation: removing this readout drops test AUC 0.897->0.869 (-0.028) - the single largest nonlinear contribution to generalisation.

parts.name: risk_aggregation_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Node 534 = ReLU(0.818*[benign_profile_gate_534path] - 0.677*[chol_threshold] - 1.155*ca - 0.592*chol - 0.761): the model's most elaborate unit, a genuine ReLU gate (hard-zero 53.5% verified) composing four risk signals - vessel count (ca), a cholesterol copy, the cholesterol threshold (3040), and the redundant benign-profile copy (155_b). Net per-unit output effects: ca +1.02, chol +0.52, chol_threshold +0.60, benign -0.72; when the benign signal is strong the whole block is clipped off together. KEY ABLATION RESULT: disabling 534's readout changes test AUC only 0.897->0.899 (+0.002) while train drops 0.946->0.942 - i.e. this showpiece unit is essentially train-only and does not generalise. Signs match cardiology but the structure is fit to the 242 training cases.
variables: number of major vessels coloured by fluoroscopy

parts.name: restbp_chol_interaction
parts.original_hypothesis: Subgraph {trestbps, chol_c, 3240, 2379}: a near-linear resting-blood-pressure signal. 3240 = ReLU(0.978*trestbps + 3.4) is always-on (100% active, verified) - a linear pass-through, not a gate. 2379 = ReLU(0.931*3240 - 0.529*chol_c - 0.754) simplifies to ReLU(0.911*trestbps - 0.529*chol_c + 2.41), near-always-on. Reads out to output with +0.364 (higher resting BP raises risk). Ablation: removing this readout drops test AUC 0.897->0.885 (-0.012) - a modest but real generalising contribution.

parts.name: chol_threshold
parts.original_hypothesis: Node 3040 = ReLU(1.052*chol - 0.864): a one-sided cholesterol threshold. Since cholesterol is z-normalised, this turns on only above ~0.82 SD above the mean. Activation profile: hard-zero 82.5% / active 17.5% (verified) - a sparse threshold detector. Feeds node 534 with -0.677; net path effect +0.60 per unit (high cholesterol raises predicted risk). This is the sub-unit that lets cholesterol act as a risk factor only above a level rather than linearly - but it sits inside the 534 gate, which the ablation shows contributes nothing on test.

parts.name: benign_profile_gate_534path
parts.original_hypothesis: Node 155_b computes the SAME benign-profile gate as 155_a (identical incoming weights and bias 0.088); it is the second copy of hidden node 155, routed into node 534 instead of the output. The benign signal is therefore encoded twice - once directly to the output (155_a) and once inside the 534 gate (155_b). 155_b enters 534 with weight +0.818; net path effect (+0.818)*(-0.884) = -0.72 per unit, same risk-lowering direction as the direct copy.

For them it clearly lowers the risk of heart disease (odds about ×0.39 on average, on the model's odds scale).

The model gives women a lower risk than men, and even more so if exercise does not bring on chest pain (odds about ×0.02 for patients without chest pain on exercise against ×0.19 for patients whose chest pain is brought on by exercise, on the model's odds scale).

The model gives patients with fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL a lower risk than patients with fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less, and even more so if exercise does not bring on chest pain (odds about ×0.11 for patients without chest pain on exercise against ×0.74 for patients whose chest pain is brought on by exercise, on the model's odds scale).

The model gives women a lower risk than men, and even more so if fasting blood sugar is above 120 mg/dL (odds about ×0.03 for patients with fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL against ×0.04 for patients with fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly gives women a lower risk through this part than men (odds about ×0.32 on average, on the model's odds scale).

The model clearly gives patients with fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL a lower risk through this part than patients with fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less (odds about ×0.36 on average, on the model's odds scale).

The model clearly gives patients whose chest pain is brought on by exercise a higher risk through this part than patients without chest pain on exercise (odds about ×2.2 on average, on the model's odds scale).

ann_36.text: This part acts on 9 of 242 training patients (4%).
For them it raises the risk of heart disease (odds about ×1.30 on average, on the model's odds scale). The model has little data on this: only 9 training patients (patients the part acts on).

Through this part, serum cholesterol only adds to the risk of heart disease once it rises above about 285 mg/dL (7.4 mmol/L) (9 training patients are past that point). The model has little data on this: only 9 training patients (of them, patients already past their fold).
